discovery: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background using pulsar timing arrays

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany (EPTA)

motivation: Decades of precision timing of millisecond pulsars, pursued by NANOGrav, EPTA and PPTA, have turned the Galaxy into a detector with a baseline of light-years. In 2023 these collaborations reported coordinated evidence for a stochastic gravitational-wave background at nanohertz frequencies, including the Hellings-Downs angular correlation that marks its gravitational origin. This opens a new window in the gravitational-wave spectrum, far below LIGO/Virgo and LISA. It tests the population of supermassive black-hole binaries and constrains early-universe sources such as cosmic strings and first-order phase transitions at the QCD scale. McLaughlin, Kramer and Manchester led the building of these timing arrays, their instrumentation, pulsar discovery and analysis methods over many years. This is the kind of patient, quantitative, community-building work that turns a theoretical possibility into a measurement, and it links particle physics and cosmology to observation.
